Issue: Attempts to collect debt not owed
Consumer complaint narrative:
b'I am filing this complaint against National Credit Adjusters, LLC ("NCA") regarding their continued attempt to collect a debt that is void and unenforceable under California law, and their repeated failure to provide adequate debt validation as required under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692g.

BACKGROUND

In approximately XXXX XXXX, NCA began reporting a collection account (Account No. XXXX original account No. XXXX) to my credit reports, claiming a balance of $XXXX. NCA placed repeated telephone calls to me beginning before I was aware of their identity. I did not recognize these calls and did not answer them.

On XXXX XXXX XXXX, I filed a dispute with XXXX regarding this account. On XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX returned the account as "VERIFIED AS ACCURATE" with no substantive explanation of how this verification was conducted. During this dispute period, NCA continued placing telephone calls to me, including documented calls on XXXX XXXX XXXX (from XXXX XXXX XXXX) and XXXX XXXX XXXX (from XXXX XXXX XXXX) two different phone numbers, both identified by caller ID as NCA. At that time, I had not yet sent NCA a direct written dispute, so I do not allege this calling activity alone violated 15 U.S.C. 1692g(b). However, this pattern of continued contact from multiple numbers during a period in which the underlying account was actively disputed with a credit bureau is relevant context for evaluating NCA's overall conduct and is documented in my records.

On XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX, NCA mailed me a letter (received XXXX XXXX XXXX, a ten-day delay for presorted first-class mail addressed to an outdated address) enclosing only the original Installment Loan Agreement, which revealed that the underlying obligation was issued by XXXX XXXX XXXX c/o XXXX on XXXX XXXX XXXX with a stated principal of $XXXX and an Annual Percentage Rate of 179.00% generating a finance charge of $XXXX.

THE UNDERLYING DEBT IS VOID UNDER CALIFORNIA LAW

California Financial Code 22303 caps interest rates on consumer installment loans under $XXXX at 36% APR. The 179.00% APR reflected in the alleged loan agreement is nearly five times this statutory cap. California Financial Code 22651 renders loans made in violation of this cap void meaning no person has the right to collect principal, charges, or recompense on the loan.

On XXXX XXXX XXXX one week after the alleged loan was purportedly originated the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX entered a Settlement Agreement against XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX License No. XXXX, citing violations of California Financial Code Sections 22303, 22304, 22304.5, 22305, and 22320.5 the exact provisions governing the rate cap applicable to this alleged obligation. This is a matter of public record, documented in XXXX official XXXX XXXX Summary of Enforcement Actions.

NCA'S VALIDATION RESPONSE WAS INADEQUATE TWICE

On XXXX XXXX XXXX I sent NCA a formal written validation demand via certified mail (delivered and signed for XXXX XXXX XXXX, tracking number XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX), disputing the validity of this alleged debt in its entirety and citing the FDCPA, the California Rosenthal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, and the void nature of the underlying obligation under California law. I specifically demanded: (1) proof of chain of title from XXXX XXXX XXXX to NCA; (2) an itemized account history explaining how the claimed balance grew from a stated principal of $XXXX to $XXXX (3) the purchase price NCA paid for this alleged debt; (4) proof of NCA's California debt collection license; and (5) the legal basis for any added interest or fees.

On XXXX XXXX XXXX, I received a second letter from NCA. This letter contained the identical documents previously sent the same cover letter format and the same Installment Loan Agreement with none of my specific demands addressed. NCA did not provide chain of title documentation, did not explain the balance discrepancy, did not provide licensing information, and did not respond in any way to the void loan argument or the XXXX enforcement action I cited and enclosed as documentation. Receipt of these documents does not constitute, and should not be construed as, an admission that this alleged debt is valid, owed, or enforceable.

This pattern of sending an identical, non-responsive packet a second time after receiving a detailed written dispute is relevant to the statutory damages factors under 15 U.S.C. 1692k(b), which directs courts to consider "the frequency and persistence of noncompliance by the debt collector" and "the extent to which such noncompliance was intentional." NCA's repetition of the same inadequate response, without engaging any of the specific legal and factual issues I raised, reflects persistent noncompliance rather than an isolated oversight.'

I also request that LVNV Funding LLC cease collection activity until this matter has been fully investigated and the requested documentation has been provided, consistent with 15 U.S.C. 1692g. Consumer complaint narrative: My name is XXXX XXXX, and I am submitting this formal complaint regarding my recent experience with the World Finance branch located at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, Missouri XXXX. I am requesting that World Finance Corporate, Compliance, and Ethics departments conduct a complete review and investigation into the handling of my personal loan application, the communication surrounding the application process, and the failure to provide me with timely and adequate information regarding the decision made on my application. On or around XX/XX/year>, I submitted an application for a personal loan in the amount of {$12000.00} through the World Finance branch located at the address listed above. I applied in good faith and provided the requested information necessary for the company to evaluate my application, including information relating to my employment, income, identity, and intended use of the requested loan proceeds. I entered into this process expecting a professional and transparent lending experience. I understand that lenders have underwriting requirements and that not every application is approved. However, regardless of the final lending decision, consumers deserve to be treated fairly, communicated with professionally, and provided with appropriate explanations when adverse decisions are made. My concern is not simply that my application was denied. My concern is the manner in which my application was handled, the lack of follow-up communication, the failure to provide the promised callback, and the absence of a clear written explanation regarding the reasons for the denial. Background Regarding My Loan Application After submitting my application, I was contacted by a World Finance representative named XXXX XXXX. During our conversation, XXXX XXXX asked me questions regarding my loan request, including questions about why I wanted the funds and what I intended to use the money for. I explained that the requested funds were for legitimate personal expenses, including repairs and maintenance related to my XXXX XXXX. Specifically, I explained that the funds were needed for necessary vehicle-related expenses, including : New tires ; Brake repairs ; Vehicle sensor repairs ; and Other maintenance-related expenses. I also provided information regarding my employment and income. I explained that I earn approximately {$5700.00} every two weeks. I answered the questions presented to me and fully cooperated throughout the process. I understand that lenders may ask questions regarding loan purpose, income, employment, and financial circumstances as part of their underwriting process. However, during the conversation, I felt that the discussion became unnecessarily focused on questioning my personal financial decisions rather than evaluating my application based on my qualifications and the information provided. I was willing to provide information necessary for the application review process, but I expected the interaction to remain professional, respectful, and focused on the actual lending criteria. Promised Callback That Never Occurred At the conclusion of my conversation with XXXX XXXX, I was specifically advised that he would call me back within approximately one hour regarding the status of my application. Based on that statement, I reasonably expected a follow-up communication regarding whether additional documentation was needed, whether my application required further review, or whether a decision had been made. However, that callback never occurred. I did not receive the promised phone call. I was not contacted by XXXX XXXX to explain the status of my application. I was not informed directly that my application had been denied. Instead, I later learned that my application had been denied without receiving the communication that had been promised to me. This lack of communication was concerning because I had taken the time to provide information, answer questions, and cooperate with the application process. At a minimum, I believe I should have received a professional follow-up explaining the outcome. Failure to Receive Written Explanation of Denial After learning that my loan application was denied, I expected to receive a written explanation identifying the reasons for the decision. As of the date of this complaint, I have not received a written adverse action notice explaining the principal reasons for the denial of my application. A consumer should not be left guessing why a financial decision was made, particularly when that decision affects access to credit. A written explanation is important because it allows consumers to : Understand the basis of the decision ; Correct possible errors ; Address issues affecting future applications ; Determine whether inaccurate information was used ; Exercise applicable consumer rights. Without a written explanation, I have no way of knowing whether the decision was based on : Credit information ; Verification issues ; Income considerations ; Documentation concerns ; Underwriting criteria ; Internal policies ; or Any other factor. I respectfully request that World Finance provide the complete adverse action notice associated with my application, including the principal reasons for the denial. Concerns Regarding Application Handling My concerns regarding this matter include, but are not limited to, the following : 1. Failure to provide promised follow-up communication I was specifically told that I would receive a callback within one hour. That communication never occurred. Consumers should not be told they will receive follow-up communication and then receive no response. 2. Lack of transparency regarding the denial decision I was denied but was not provided with a clear explanation of why the application was declined. A transparent lending process requires that consumers understand the basis for significant financial decisions. 3. Lack of professionalism during the application review While I understand that lenders may ask questions about loan purpose and financial circumstances, I felt the conversation became unnecessarily focused on challenging my personal reasons for requesting the loan rather than objectively reviewing my application. 4. Concern regarding whether proper procedures were followed I am requesting that World Finance review whether the application was processed consistently with company policies and applicable consumer lending requirements. Request for Internal Investigation I respectfully request that World Finance conduct a formal internal investigation into this matter. As part of that investigation, I request review of : My complete loan application file ; The underwriting decision ; The decision timeline ; Internal notes ; Communication records ; Telephone recordings, if available ; Employee notes ; System records ; Any internal messages regarding my application; Any documentation relied upon in making the lending decision. I specifically request that World Finance preserve all records relating to my application while this complaint is under review. This preservation request includes : Call recordings ; Application records ; Underwriting documentation ; Credit decision records ; Internal communications ; Emails ; Text messages ; Employee notes ; Time stamps showing application review activity ; Approval or denial records. Request for Complete Loan File Documentation I respectfully request copies of all documents associated with my application, including : Application submission records ; Documents provided during the application process ; Verification records ; Underwriting notes ; Decision records ; Adverse action notice ; Reason codes ; Any communications related to the denial. Providing these records will allow me to better understand the decision-making process and determine whether any errors occurred. Fair Lending Concerns I want to make clear that I am requesting an investigation into the handling of my application and the consistency of the process. I am not making unsupported conclusions regarding the reason for the denial. However, I believe it is appropriate for World Finance to review whether my application was handled consistently with the treatment of similarly situated applicants. If any factor other than legitimate underwriting criteria influenced the handling of my application, I request that World Finance identify and address that issue. A fair lending review should examine whether : Similar applications were evaluated using consistent standards ; The same documentation requirements were applied ; Communication procedures were followed consistently ; The decision was based on legitimate lending factors. Request for CFPB Review I am also submitting this matter to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ) because I believe additional oversight is appropriate due to : Lack of communication after the promised callback ; Failure to provide a clear explanation of the denial ; Concerns regarding transparency in the lending process ; The inability to understand what factors resulted in the adverse decision. I respectfully request that the CFPB assist in obtaining : A copy of the adverse action notice ; An explanation of the denial ; Confirmation that proper procedures were followed ; A review of whether the application was handled fairly. Request for Missouri Division of Finance Review I am requesting that the Missouri Division of Finance review this matter to determine whether World Finance followed applicable Missouri lending requirements and consumer protection standards. My concern is not that a lender declined my application. My concern is that the process lacked transparency and communication. Consumers deserve : Clear communication ; Professional treatment ; Accurate information ; Proper documentation ; An explanation of adverse decisions. Requested Resolution To resolve this matter, I respectfully request that World Finance : Conduct a complete investigation into the handling of my loan application. Review all available call recordings and employee notes related to my conversation with XXXX XXXX. Provide a copy of my complete loan application file. Provide the written adverse action notice explaining the principal reasons for the denial. Explain the specific factors that resulted in the denial of my {$12000.00} loan application. Confirm whether my application was reviewed according to standard underwriting procedures. Preserve all records related to my application. Provide a written response detailing the findings of the investigation. Correct any errors identified during the review process. Ensure that future applicants receive appropriate communication regarding application decisions. Conclusion I respectfully request that World Finance take this complaint seriously and conduct a meaningful review of what occurred. I understand that lenders have the right to approve or deny applications based on legitimate underwriting standards. My concern is not simply the denial itself. My concern is the lack of transparency, the failure to provide the promised callback, the lack of communication regarding the decision, and the absence of a written explanation allowing me to understand why my application was declined. I made a good-faith effort to provide accurate information, cooperate with the application process, and answer all questions presented to me. I believe I deserve the same level of professionalism and transparency in return. I respectfully request a written response explaining the results of your investigation and providing the requested documentation. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your timely response.

On XX/XX/year>, I submitted a formal written Debt Validation Request explicitly demanding three specific categories of records : ( 1 ) A complete transaction history and itemized accounting explaining the calculation of the alleged {$550.00} balance ; ( 2 ) Documentation supporting the underlying consumer obligation with the original creditor ; and ( 3 ) Documentation establishing Caine & Weiners legal authority to collect and furnish information concerning this specific account. Under CFPB Regulation F ( 12 CFR 1006.34 ), a debt collector must provide a consumer with clear, itemized data if requested. Caine & Weiners mailed response completely failed to meet these mandates. Furthermore, demanding a balance that relies on un-itemized, hidden 'adjustments ' constitutes a direct violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692e ( 2 ) ( A ) for misrepresenting the true legal character, nature, and amount of an alleged consumer debt. The response references a servicing timeline but does not specifically identify every reporting field currently being transmitted to XXXX XXXX XXXX, and XXXX. My dispute concerns whether each of the following reporting fields remains accurate today : Current balance. Account status. Collection status. Date opened. Date assigned. Date of first delinquency. Date of default. Payment history. Monthly payment. Current reporting codes. Remarks. Collection designation. Portfolio type. Responsibility code. Compliance condition code. Special comment code. Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint against Transunion for a willful violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681i, based on its failure to conduct a reasonable investigation into a disputed collection account. I previously disputed the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX collection account ( account ending in XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) under Transunion File Identification Number # XXXX. Despite my dispute, Transunion marked the account as " Verified '' without obtaining competent evidence that the account actually belongs to me. Attached are the documents that were provided to me through my CFPB complaint response from the debt collector. Those documents consist of the Bill of Sale, the referenced " Schedule A '' for the " XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, '' and account statements. These are the same documents the debt collector relied upon to support its claim of ownership. The debt collector 's purported proof of ownership consists only of a bulk asset purchase agreement, including the Bill of Sale and the referenced Schedule A. However, the Bill of Sale expressly states that the specific account information is contained in separate electronic spreadsheet files. Those spreadsheet files which should identify the individual accounts included in the sale have never been produced by either the debt collector or Transunion . As a result, there is no evidence demonstrating that this alleged account was included in the portfolio that was supposedly transferred. Neither Transunion nor the furnisher has produced any document showing my name, Social Security number, account number, or any other identifying information linking me to the alleged debt through the referenced transfer documents. While account statements may show information relating to an alleged underlying account, they do not establish that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX acquired this specific account through the referenced portfolio sale. Without the spreadsheet or other account-level transfer records identified in the Bill of Sale, there is no evidence connecting this alleged account to the purchased portfolio. By verifying this account based solely on a generic purchase agreement that depends entirely on missing, unproduced spreadsheets, Transunion failed to conduct the reasonable investigation required by 15 U.S.C. 1681i. A reasonable investigation requires confirming that the disputed account is actually included in the referenced records and that the information being reported is supported by competent evidence. Simply accepting the furnisher 's unsupported assertion or relying on incomplete documentation does not satisfy Transunion 's statutory obligations. Transunion 's decision to continue reporting this account as verified despite the absence of documentation identifying this account within the transferred portfolio demonstrates a failure to maintain the maximum possible accuracy of the information in my credit file, as required by the FCRA. This constitutes a willful or, at a minimum, negligent failure to comply with its duties under the Act.
